For Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Apple TV, JioHotstar and other streaming apps, the Top Shelf shows backdrops of shows currently on that service, from tvmaze.com (refreshed twice a day). Android only lets its built-in launcher read the apps\' own posters.
Make Glass your permanent Home screen and clean up preinstalled apps.
Lock Glass as the main launcher

Sets Glass as the default Home app, turns off the original launcher and switches on Home Guard. Needs USB debugging on (see How this works). Accept the \"Allow debugging?\" prompt and tick Always allow.
Opens Accessibility settings. Choose Glass Launcher Home Guard and turn it on. Home Guard sends the Home button back to Glass and closes the original launcher whenever it appears.
Select apps, then press Disable. Disabled apps disappear completely but are not deleted, so you can bring them back here at any time.
No preinstalled extras were found on this TV.

Locking Glass and removing bloatware use the TV's own debugging connection, the same access a PC gets with adb.

1. Settings → Device Preferences (or System) → About: press OK on Build 7 times.
2. Settings → Developer options: turn on USB debugging, and Network debugging if your TV lists it.
3. Come back here, press a button, and accept the "Allow debugging?" prompt (tick Always allow).

If it says it can't connect, your TV only offers Wireless debugging. From a PC, run "adb connect TV-IP" once, then "adb tcpip 5555", and try again. Needs Android 8 or newer.
